steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Exam structure: 2 hours, 100 marks. Section A - Core Technical Principles (20 marks, short answer), Section B - Specialist Technical Principles (30 marks, short and extended), Section C - Designing and Making Principles (50 marks, extended response).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Command words: 'State' - brief factual answer (1-2 marks). 'Describe' - say what happens (2-4 marks). 'Explain' - describe AND give reasons (3-6 marks). 'Evaluate' - give both sides and reach a justified conclusion (6-10 marks). 'Justify' - give reasons for your choice (4-6 marks).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Time management: 2 hours for 100 marks = 1.2 minutes per mark. Section A: 24 minutes. Section B: 36 minutes. Section C: 60 minutes. Leave 10 minutes for checking.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Section C strategy: this section tests AO3 most heavily - worth 50 marks. Read the context carefully, identify the user and their needs, use the SEE framework (Social, Economic, Environmental) for evaluation, always justify conclusions with specific evidence.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between the command words 'describe' and 'evaluate', giving an example of how your answer would differ for each. | A question asks: 'Evaluate the suitability of using polypropylene for a reusable food container.' Write a plan for a full-mark answer. | A student writes one-sided answers that only give advantages. Explain why this loses marks and how they should improve.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'Describe' = say what happens or what something is like. E.g. 'PP is a thermoplastic that can be melted and reshaped, is lightweight and chemical-resistant' - factual, no judgement. 'Evaluate' = give  | Plan: 1) Define PP and its key properties (thermoplastic, food-safe grades, chemical resistant, lightweight, microwave-safe PP5, low cost). 2) Advantages for food container: food-safe, chemical resist | Evaluation requires BOTH sides - advantages AND disadvantages - plus a justified conclusion. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the command word FIRST - it tells you how much depth is needed For 'evaluate' questions, always give a BALANCED answer: advantages, disadvantages, conclusion For Section C, annotate the context sheet - highlight user needs and constraints
